title: Static asset manifest path/content root confusion could expose files outside intended web root
attacker_control: HTTP request path to a configured static asset endpoint; no evidence that a remote attacker controls the manifest path or content root in default runtime.
attacker_privileges: Unauthenticated remote web client against an app that has called MapStaticAssets.
victim_and_owner: Application host filesystem and static web root owned by the app/developer.
prerequisites: Attacker can request paths served by the app
security_invariant: A web client must not be able to select arbitrary files outside the app's configured static asset roots.
suspected_root_cause: If manifest path or content roots were lower-trust, descriptor AssetPath lookup might reach unintended file providers.
sensitive_sink: IFileProvider.GetFileInfo and static file response body serving.
boundary: Remote web client -> application filesystem read authority.
expected_impact: Unauthorized local file disclosure outside intended static assets.
validation_plan: Trace whether request path influences manifest path
Trace whether request path influences content root
Check whether file provider root checks are bypassed
negative_controls: FileProvider lookup remains under configured root
evidence: Manual source trace found manifest path is supplied by app/developer and relative paths are resolved below AppContext.BaseDirectory; request path does not select manifest path.
Manifest file providers are built from manifest content roots rather than direct request path roots.
triage_objections: The attacker controls only HTTP request path, not the manifest path/content root authority needed for the hypothesized arbitrary file read.
triage_rounds: Round 1: rejected because the source trace did not show lower-trust control of manifest path/content root or observable file disclosure.
notes: Useful hardening review target, but not a reportable vulnerability based on available evidence.

title: CI archive extraction or script execution could cross from contributor input to release authority
attacker_control: Potential contributor-controlled repository changes or build inputs in CI; exact protected workflow path not proven.
attacker_privileges: Malicious contributor or fork PR author.
victim_and_owner: Repository CI/release secrets, signed artifacts, package publishing authority.
prerequisites: Authorized controlled fork/runner or CI simulation
security_invariant: Untrusted contribution code must not execute with secrets, signing, release, or protected repository write authority.
suspected_root_cause: Archive extraction or script execution may be reachable in a privileged workflow without sufficient trust separation.
sensitive_sink: Build script execution, extracted tools, CI tokens/secrets/artifacts.
expected_impact: Protected workflow command execution or artifact substitution.
validation_plan: Use controlled fork/runner with dummy secrets
Prove or disprove secret/artifact authority transition
evidence: Read-only search found archive extraction and process execution in engineering scripts, but no protected workflow exploit path was locally demonstrated.
triage_objections: Without a controlled authorized CI environment and workflow permission proof, this remains a supply-chain review lead rather than a vulnerability.
notes: Carry forward for a dedicated CI/release audit.
